problem:
$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]x(t),\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4\end{aligned}],\,x(t)={e}^{-t}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -4\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem and its solution given above. What is the tangent vector to the solution curve at the point corresponding to $t=\operatorname{ln}⁡3?$
worked_solution:
Recall that the $xy$-coordinate plane is called the *phase plane* of the system. A particular solution of an initial value problem is called a *trajectory* (or *orbit*).

First, we compute the point that corresponds to $t=\operatorname{ln}⁡3$ on the given trajectory:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(\operatorname{ln}⁡3) & ={e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{e}^{2(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+9[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -36\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} \\ -36\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the equation of our system, we obtain the tangent vector to the trajectory.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(\operatorname{ln}⁡3) & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} \\ -36\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(-1)(\frac{2}{3})+0(-36) \\ 0\cdot (\frac{2}{3})+2(-36)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{3} \\ -72\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
